walkthrough: Goal: V大's weeks 3 and 4 assignment, 画面分割 and 整图复制: a whole picture's most obvious divisions found by feel (squinting, never by analysis) and drawn beside it in three levels, red, green and blue; then a whole picture copied at low completion on top of its own division, dimmed. Nothing is scored: the picture laid in place under my lines is the check, the card only counts and measures what I drew (V大's at most five main lines, as long as they run).
Before the pack: Stage 4 · Simplifying in the practice options starts a stage-4 session of S94's mix, objects first, as it did: without the composition pack there is no division or whole copy.

The pack: Import practice pack… in the practice options, the composition pack chosen in the picker: the notice says what its pictures are for; its row reads its title and how many pictures, no outlines (a composition is never outlined). Stage 4's row now has three tiles in pencil: Objects, Division (a picture's edge with a long line through it, another meeting it and a small frame) and Whole copy (the same edge with a hill's line and a house).

Division: a drill of three compositions on a sheet of its own, the simple and medium tiers in turn, none twice; its How first. Title: Divide a picture; Weeks 3 and 4 · a whole picture's few big divisions found by squinting, drawn beside it in three levels. The example, a landscape of a few masses generated without a pack (sky, a ridge, a field, a tree and a house), plays beside its picture, whose edge my frame shows: first the ridge's turning point, then the two longest lines red through the picture; from them each part's frame green (the tree's, the house's); then shorter still blue (the roof, the door, the path); Compare: the picture faint under the lines, the lines in their colours. Steps: 1 Squint: the few most obvious lines, red, right through, 2 From them, each part's frame, green, 3 Shorter still, blue, 4 Compare. One paragraph: about half the time on the red lines, no right or wrong but roughly the same as others see it, small turns ignored, a bent line's turning point first, the canvas not zoomed in; red, green and blue are the levels' colours, Compare lays the picture under my lines, the slider setting how strongly it shows.

The exercise: the picture in the original's frame with its credit small under it; my frame holds only the picture's edge in pencil, the empty frame of its size. The tools: Main (red), Second (green), Third (blue), Undo, Redo; no Sketch, no Draw, no Correct. Strokes of a level whose ends meet within two pen widths heading on are one line: a long line may be drawn in pieces.

I draw the two main lines in red right through the picture, the ridge bent at its peak in one stroke and the field's edge in two pieces that meet; then with Second the house's frame in three strokes and two sides of the tree's; then with Third the door, the window and the path's two edges stopping short of the door. Compare: the picture lies in place under my lines at half strength, the lines in their colours as thick as the pen, round at their turns and ends; the card is its title, the slider Original shown (50 %, as a whole copy's) and under it a table of the three levels: each level's colour as a short line, the lines drawn (Main 2, Second 5, Third 4) and how far they run on average as a share of the picture's longer side (the bent ridge longer than the side). The record keeps these first numbers, shown nowhere else. A dark picture would read poorly at half: I set the slider most of the way, the picture stronger under the same lines, the table unchanged.

Lines drawn after Compare are part of the division (the pen stays a level's, no Correct): I add four more main lines, one ending in a small hook turned back and one running on past my frame's bottom edge; the comparison goes as my pen lands; Compare again: the overlay laid anew as strongly as I left it, the hook round with no spike, the long line stopping at my frame's edge as its ink does, nothing over the frame or the card (pinched in on the two, the hook's end round, the long line cut at the frame); Main 6 in red on the card (V大: at most five). Undo and Redo as any stroke.
Next, Next, Finish: Division drill done, its sheet small with my division beside the first picture. Back in the options Division is inked.

Whole copy: a drill of one; its How first. Title: Copy a whole picture; Weeks 3 and 4 · a division continued into a copy of the whole picture, big shapes right, no details. The example: the division drawn red and green, then Draw: the division dims and the line drawing goes over it in ink; Compare: the picture laid over my copy, the division gone. Steps: 1 Divide it: red, then green, 2 Draw: the big shapes over it, no details, 3 Compare.

The exercise: a picture not shown in the division drill (none from the last ten sessions while others are left). The tools: Main, Second, Third, Draw, Undo, Redo. I divide it in red and green (the ridge and the field's edge, the tree's and the house's frames); I choose Draw: my division dims under it; I draw the big shapes' lines in ink over it, the ridge's peak a little too high. Compare: the picture in place over my copy as strongly as the slider Original shown sets (half at first), my division hidden; the card its title and the slider; at most of the way the picture nearly covers my lines, the peak's error plain. Undo takes back my last line only, the division still hidden while compared. Finish: Whole copy drill done.

With the pack, Stage 4 · Simplifying starts stage 4's session of the new mix: after a warm-up of the kinds met (none of these; divisions and whole copies never warm up), three objects, a division and a whole copy, about 30 to 32 minutes; Next past the objects: Division 1 of 1 (its How first on a session's sheet, as every kind compared only in a drill), an upright picture of the medium tier; then Whole copy 1 of 1 of the simple tier, one of the drills' again as all three simple ones were shown in the last ten sessions.
In Chinese (s95-division-zh, this walk-through run as on a Chinese tablet): 画面分割, 整图复制; the pens 主分割, 次分割, 三级, 画图笔; the table's 条数 and 平均长度; the canvas's hashes are this run's.
Not here: the author's hand on the tablet; Notan and colour blocks (the next slice); a session walked to its end (its objects are S94's).
